messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, balance_gain, freq, kd, torso_mass, foot_length, leg_density, torque_limit, hip_amp, ramp_s, pitch_kp, kp, knee_amp, foot_friction
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): fp_kd, duty, start_lean, sync_gain, knee_shift, stance_knee, fp_kv, hip_bias, pitch_ref
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, com_vx_mean, flight_fraction, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, saturation_frac_hip, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, com_vx_slope, slip_fraction, double_support_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_slope, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, pitch_slope, step_length_over_L, pitch_mean, swing_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, com_height_over_L_slope, step_freq_hz, pre_fall.pitch, n_walking, pre_fall.com_vx, capture_margin_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, saturation_frac_knee, pitch_rate_slope, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.slip_fraction, saturation_frac_ankle, pitch_rate_end, com_height_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, tracking_error_ankle, capture_margin_over_L_mean, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, tracking_error_knee, angmom_norm_slope, angmom_norm_mean, pitch_rate_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, capture_inside_fraction, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, com_vx_end, pitch_end, friction_utilisation_p95, fall_time, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, tracking_error_hip, n_fell, angmom_norm_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pre_fall.angmom_norm, time_upright, pre_fall.pitch_rate. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

STEP 1 of at most 12. Model requests used so far: 0 of 24.
Rollout budget: 696 remaining of 700; n_obs = 4, n_train = 4.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): leg_length, balance_gain, freq, kd, torso_mass, foot_length, leg_density, torque_limit, hip_amp, ramp_s, pitch_kp, kp, knee_amp, foot_friction
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): fp_kd, duty, start_lean, sync_gain, knee_shift, stance_knee, fp_kv, hip_bias, pitch_ref
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, com_vx_mean, flight_fraction, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, saturation_frac_hip, com_height_over_L_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, com_vx_slope, slip_fraction, double_support_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_slope, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, pitch_slope, step_length_over_L, pitch_mean, swing_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, com_height_over_L_slope, step_freq_hz, pre_fall.pitch, n_walking, pre_fall.com_vx, capture_margin_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, saturation_frac_knee, pitch_rate_slope, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.slip_fraction, saturation_frac_ankle, pitch_rate_end, com_height_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, tracking_error_ankle, capture_margin_over_L_mean, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, tracking_error_knee, angmom_norm_slope, angmom_norm_mean, pitch_rate_mean, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, capture_inside_fraction, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, com_vx_end, pitch_end, friction_utilisation_p95, fall_time, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, tracking_error_hip, n_fell, angmom_norm_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, pre_fall.angmom_norm, time_upright, pre_fall.pitch_rate. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. messages.content:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): balance_gain, torque_limit, knee_amp, kd, leg_length, kp, freq, foot_friction, hip_amp, foot_length, torso_mass, ramp_s, pitch_kp, leg_density
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): fp_kd, duty, hip_bias, sync_gain, pitch_ref, knee_shift, fp_kv, stance_knee, start_lean
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: capture_margin_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, flight_fraction, pitch_end, pitch_rate_slope, double_support_fraction, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, step_freq_hz, saturation_frac_knee, slip_fraction, com_height_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, tracking_error_knee, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.slip_fraction, angmom_norm_slope, friction_utilisation_p95, tracking_error_ankle, pre_fall.pitch, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, pre_fall.com_vx, tracking_error_hip, angmom_norm_mean, saturation_frac_hip, swing_clearance_min_over_L, saturation_frac_ankle, n_walking, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_end, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pre_fall.angmom_norm, n_fell, capture_margin_over_L_slope, com_vx_mean, time_upright, step_length_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_vx_slope, pitch_rate_mean, pitch_slope, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, fall_time, com_vx_end, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pitch_mean, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, capture_inside_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_mean, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, angmom_norm_end, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

final.explanation: The primary symptom is an excessively high step frequency combined with short step length, indicating the robot is stepping too fast for its leg length. This generates insufficient forward foot placement and allows the center of mass to advance beyond the base of support, producing a large negative capture margin and forward falls. Reducing the commanded frequency (via the timing tool) should lengthen steps and improve stability; augmenting foot‑placement gains (via the placement tool) can provide additional corrective action if needed.

H1.causal_chain: High freq → high step frequency → insufficient time for foot to swing forward → short step length and low forward foot placement → COM moves ahead of support point → capture margin becomes negative large → forward fall.
H1.mechanism: The commanded gait frequency (freq) is too high relative to the leg's natural pendulum dynamics, producing excessively rapid strides.

H2.causal_chain: Low fp_kd/fp_kv → weak corrective swing‑foot placement → foot lands too close to or behind the COM → insufficient braking impulse → COM drifts forward → capture margin negative → forward fall.
H2.mechanism: Foot placement gains (fp_kd, fp_kv) are too low to generate adequate forward foot placement against the robot's forward momentum.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): balance_gain, torque_limit, knee_amp, kd, leg_length, kp, freq, foot_friction, hip_amp, foot_length, torso_mass, ramp_s, pitch_kp, leg_density
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): fp_kd, duty, hip_bias, sync_gain, pitch_ref, knee_shift, fp_kv, stance_knee, start_lean
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: capture_margin_over_L_end, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, flight_fraction, pitch_end, pitch_rate_slope, double_support_fraction, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, step_freq_hz, saturation_frac_knee, slip_fraction, com_height_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, tracking_error_knee, pitch_rate_end, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.slip_fraction, angmom_norm_slope, friction_utilisation_p95, tracking_error_ankle, pre_fall.pitch, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, pre_fall.com_vx, tracking_error_hip, angmom_norm_mean, saturation_frac_hip, swing_clearance_min_over_L, saturation_frac_ankle, n_walking, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, com_height_over_L_end, pre_fall.pitch_rate, pre_fall.angmom_norm, n_fell, capture_margin_over_L_slope, com_vx_mean, time_upright, step_length_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, com_vx_slope, pitch_rate_mean, pitch_slope, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean, fall_time, com_vx_end, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, pitch_mean, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, capture_inside_fraction, capture_margin_over_L_mean, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, angmom_norm_end, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02.

final.explanation: The strongest quantitative deviation from healthy ranges is the knee torque saturation fraction, which is two orders of magnitude above the healthy norm while other quantities (step length, COM height, pitch) are also abnormal in the direction expected when forward propulsion is limited. This points to insufficient torque authority as the primary cause of the backward fall. Secondary symptoms such as low step length and negative capture margin are consistent with, and may be exacerbated by, poor foot placement, hence a second repair targeting placement gains is proposed.

H1.causal_chain: Low torque_limit → knee torque demand exceeds available torque → saturation_frac_knee rises → net forward acceleration reduced → COM moves backward, pitch leans backward, step length shrinks → fall backward.
H1.mechanism: Insufficient actuator torque authority at the knee joint causes torque saturation during stance, limiting forward propulsive force and resulting in backward falls and short steps.

H2.causal_chain: Low fp_kd and/or fp_kv → foot lands posterior to COM → capture point moves outside support interval (negative capture_margin_over_L) → backward toppling moment → pitch backs up, COM moves backward → fall.
H2.mechanism: Inadequate foot‑placement gains place the swing foot too far behind the centre of mass, providing insufficient forward base of support and allowing the capture point to drift outside the support region, which drives a backward fall.

policy_record.system_prompt:
You are a causal engineering scientist. A bipedal robot simulated in MuJoCo, which is known to have walked well in some earlier configuration, now fails to walk. Your job: find out WHY it fails, by experiment, then direct a repair that is checked by an independent verification you cannot see. The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): kp, torso_mass, ramp_s, kd, foot_friction, leg_length, balance_gain, torque_limit, leg_density, pitch_kp, hip_amp, foot_length, knee_amp, freq
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): fp_kd, start_lean, fp_kv, pitch_ref, stance_knee, knee_shift, sync_gain, hip_bias, duty
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. Quantities you may predict: swing_clearance_min_over_L, fall_time, time_upright, swing_peak_clearance_min_over_L, pre_fall.saturation_frac_ankle, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_mean, pre_fall.com_height_over_L, saturation_frac_ankle, tracking_error_ankle, n_fell, capture_margin_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_slope, swing_peak_clearance_mean_over_L, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_slope, angmom_norm_slope, pitch_slope, com_height_over_L_mean, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_end, cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L_end, pre_fall.com_vx, pitch_end, com_height_over_L_end, friction_utilisation_p95, pre_fall.slip_fraction, angmom_norm_mean, saturation_frac_knee, com_vx_end, max_friction_utilisation, pre_fall.saturation_frac_hip, pre_fall.pitch, pitch_rate_mean, pre_fall.pitch_rate, com_vx_slope, flight_fraction, pre_fall.capture_margin_over_L, com_height_over_L_slope, capture_inside_fraction, pre_fall.cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L, pitch_rate_slope, pre_fall.saturation_frac_knee, pitch_mean, step_freq_hz, double_support_fraction, pre_fall.max_friction_utilisation, step_length_over_L, tracking_error_hip, n_walking, saturation_frac_hip, angmom_norm_end, tracking_error_knee, pre_fall.angmom_norm, capture_margin_over_L_end, pitch_rate_end, slip_fraction, com_vx_mean, capture_margin_over_L_slope, pre_fall.com_ahead_of_cop_over_L, com_ahead_of_cop_over_L_mean. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

PROTOCOL. A single reply: JSON object following the response schema, no prose. Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. The repairs you list are run in order from the current best design; their budget shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at your decision and must sum to at most 1.

The GOAL is a design that genuinely walks in that hidden verification: a correct diagnosis alone repairs nothing, and concluding before any repair has improved the robot submits the unchanged, failing robot. In this session you answer ONCE, from the initial observation only: you receive no experimental feedback. Give your hypotheses and up to two repairs.

INSTRUMENTS AND COSTS (one shared rollout budget; every instrument call is charged before it runs):
- observation: the initial physics observation of the robot (already done; its cost is spent). Rollouts are 10 s simulated walks on a fixed set of observation seeds with random initial perturbations and floor friction variation.
- counterfactual: an experiment you design. Apply ONE or TWO parameter changes (two different parameters: an interaction test) to the CURRENT BEST design and re-observe it on the SAME observation seeds, everything else held fixed. Cost n_obs rollouts (2 x n_obs if the current best design has not yet been observed, because it is observed first). You get the measured change of every summary quantity and the new falls. A counterfactual is a measurement, not a repair: it never changes the current best design. A counterfactual action may hold one or two experiments, run in order. Each change is {param, level}:
- multiplicative parameters (levels x0.33, x0.5, x0.7, x0.85, x1.2, x1.5, x2, x3: the value is multiplied by the factor): torque_limit, foot_length, hip_amp, ramp_s, knee_amp, freq, leg_length, leg_density, balance_gain, foot_friction, torso_mass, kp, kd, pitch_kp
- additive parameters (levels -0.2R, -0.1R, -0.05R, +0.05R, +0.1R, +0.2R: the value moves by that signed fraction of the parameter's allowed range R; these may be negative or sit at 0): stance_knee, pitch_ref, hip_bias, sync_gain, fp_kd, start_lean, knee_shift, duty, fp_kv
- body parameter leg_length scales thigh and shank of both legs together; foot_length scales both feet.
- each message lists every parameter's current value and allowed range. A change that would leave the allowed range is refused (never clipped) and costs nothing.
- test: a 20 s stress test of the CURRENT BEST design on the observation seeds (twice the training horizon, same perturbations); cost 2 x n_obs rollouts; once per design. Before it runs you predict how many of the n_obs seeds will walk for the whole 20 s. It changes nothing; it measures robustness on visible seeds.
- repair: a CMA-ES search over the dimensions of ONE tool, starting from the current best design, scored on training seeds. Cost = the budget you grant it = floor(budget_share x remaining rollouts); it must reach the tool's minimum budget (shown in each message) or it is refused. A repair that improves the training result (more walking seeds, then more surviving seeds, then fitness) becomes the new current best design. A repair action may contain one or two repairs, run in order; their budget_shares are fractions of the rollouts remaining at that step and must sum to at most 1. Tools:
- feedback: control parameters for the balance and pitch feedback gains; searched parameters: kp, kd, balance_gain, pitch_kp, sync_gain
- placement: the two swing-foot placement gains; searched parameters: fp_kd, fp_kv
- stride: control parameters for stride amplitude; searched parameters: hip_amp, knee_amp, ramp_s
- foot_length: the foot length (body); searched parameters: foot_length
- leg_length: thigh and shank length (body); searched parameters: thigh_length, shank_length
- torso_mass: the torso mass (body); searched parameters: torso_mass
- timing: control parameters for stride frequency, duty and knee timing; searched parameters: freq, duty, knee_shift
- torque_limit: the joint torque limit (body); searched parameters: torque_limit
- posture: control parameters for the trunk/hip posture trim; searched parameters: hip_bias, pitch_ref, stance_knee, start_lean
- foot_friction: the foot friction coefficient (body); searched parameters: foot_friction
- conclude: stop. Available once at least one repair has been attempted (or when no repair is affordable any more). The design submitted is always the best training design found so far ("best").

BUDGET. All instruments share one rollout budget; the exact costs are stated in every message (a counterfactual costs n_obs rollouts; a repair costs the budget you grant it, at least the tool's minimum). A repair's budget sets how many CMA-ES generations it runs (about budget / (n_train x population); the minimum is 3 generations). Rollouts still unused when you conclude have no value: the result is judged only by the hidden verification of the submitted design.

VERIFICATION (fixed rule full_recovery_v1, applied after you conclude; its seeds are hidden): the submitted design counts as recovered only if (1) at least 80% of 24 fresh 10 s rollouts walk, under the same kind of random perturbations and floor friction variation as training; (2) it is a statistically verified improvement over the original robot on those seeds; and (3) at least 80% of 24 further 20 s rollouts walk, with sufficient median speed and no body dragging. Training uses only n_train = 4 seeds of 10 s, so walking on all training seeds is necessary but far from sufficient. A repair's train_fitness keeps rising with more CMA-ES generations after all training seeds walk; it is the only robustness signal available before verification.

KEY FACTS AND HEALTHY REFERENCE. Each message starts the observation with computed facts (fall direction per seed in words, fall times, cadence, the pendulum frequency sqrt(g/L)/(2 pi) of the leg, Froude number, saturation, slip) and, for the main quantities, the range p10-p90 measured with the same instruments on verified-walking robots of other shapes. These are measurements and calculations; they do not say what is wrong. Being outside the healthy range is a symptom, not a cause.

PHYSICS QUANTITIES. Sign conventions: pitch and pitch_rate are positive for forward lean; angmom_norm is positive for forward rotation; com_ahead_of_cop_over_L is positive when the centre of mass is ahead of the centre of pressure; capture_margin_over_L is positive when the capture point lies inside the support interval and negative outside; cp_ahead_of_front_edge_over_L is positive when the capture point is beyond the front (toe) edge. Quantities with the prefix pre_fall. are averages over the 0.5 s before the fall and are None for seeds that did not fall. A healthy walker's capture point often lies ahead of its support interval during normal stepping, so trends, pre-fall values and changes against the robot's own baseline are more informative than absolute levels. The keys of the observation are documented in each message.

HYPOTHESES. Keep a ledger. Each hypothesis has a mechanism in words, a causal chain (how the mechanism produces the observed symptoms), a category, cited evidence paths and a status: open, supported, refuted or unresolved. Several subsystems can sometimes compensate for one fault, and one symptom can have several causes, so a repair that works does not by itself identify the cause. A hypothesis must make falsifiable predictions; revise its status when the measurements contradict them (cite the experiment ids). A refuted hypothesis cannot be re-opened; propose a new one instead. Confidence values you give are recorded but never used by any decision rule. Evidence paths (the response schema lists every valid one) are named like this: robot.body.<parameter>, robot.controller.<parameter>, robot.features.<feature>, reference.features.<feature>, observation.median.<key>, observation.pre_fall.<key> (the key without its pre_fall. prefix), observation.n_walking, observation.n_fell, experiments.<E#>.delta.<quantity> (measured change of a quantity in counterfactual E#), experiments.<E#>.n_walking, experiments.<E#>.n_fell, tests.<T#>.n_walking, tests.<T#>.n_fell, repairs.<R#>.budget, repairs.<R#>.start_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_walking, repairs.<R#>.train_fitness. Only values that exist are citable.

PREDICTIONS. Before each counterfactual you register, per hypothesis, the direction (increase, decrease, no_change) of named quantities. They are logged before the experiment runs and scored afterwards: the observed direction is the sign of the measured change beyond a tolerance, so a change smaller than the tolerance counts as no_change. n_walking, n_fell: exact (tolerance 0). Others: max(absolute, 5 % of the baseline value); absolute tolerances: fall_time and time_upright 0.25 s; any *_slope 0.005; pitch_rate 0.05 rad/s; pitch 0.02 rad; tracking_error 0.005 rad; friction_utilisation 0.05; fractions and saturation_frac 0.02; step_freq_hz 0.15 Hz; com_vx 0.05 m/s; *_over_L and angmom_norm 0.02; anything else 0.02. Predicting a quantity that is undefined (None) in the baseline or the intervention is not scored. For a repair you predict the number of training seeds walked afterwards.

DIAGNOSIS CATEGORIES (physical mechanisms; use "unresolved" if the evidence does not decide):
- weak_balance_feedback: insufficient balance feedback
- short_support_base: insufficient support base (feet too short)
- poor_foot_placement: inadequate foot placement against forward momentum
- heavy_upper_body: excessive or high upper-body mass
- leg_geometry_mismatch: leg geometry mismatch
- low_torque_authority: insufficient actuator torque authority
- cadence_too_fast: step cadence too fast for the leg
- low_traction: insufficient foot traction (slipping)
- posture_bias: forward lean / posture bias
- low_joint_impedance: joint impedance too low
- gait_initiation_failure: gait initiation failure
- unresolved: unresolved

You may conclude at any time, including immediately if you judge that no further experiment is worth its cost. A repair should follow evidence. Do not assume any particular intervention or tool will work; the evidence decides.

Write it in the schema's order: first observation_reading (what the initial observation shows physically, with numbers), then hypotheses, then repairs. final.explanation: The dominant symptom is excessive step frequency and length caused by low leg inertial density, which drives the COM forward faster than balance corrections can compensate. Addressing balance feedback and reducing knee amplitude should restore stable walking.

H1.causal_chain: Low leg density → higher leg swing speed → increased step frequency and step length → COM advances faster than the capture point can track → capture margin becomes negative (forward instability) → forward fall.
H1.mechanism: Low leg density reduces inertial resistance of the swinging legs, allowing them to accelerate too quickly.

H2.causal_chain: Low balance_gain → weak ankle/hip torque response to forward COM‑COP error → inability to shift COP forward enough to keep capture point inside support → capture margin stays negative → forward fall.
H2.mechanism: Insufficient balance feedback gain fails to generate adequate corrective torques when the COM moves ahead of the COP.

H3.causal_chain: High knee_amp → foot swings forward with low clearance (toe drag) → reduced effective step length and delayed foot placement → forward COM momentum not arrested → capture margin negative → forward fall.
H3.mechanism: Excessive knee swing amplitude produces long, low‑clearance foot trajectories that scrape the toe and reduce effective foot placement.
